props.classMechanic_text:
THE TRADE POINTS

Merchant Class – Core Mechanic

Trade Points (TP) are a Merchant’s currency of favors, contacts, and market leverage. Use them to grease wheels, open doors, and conjure goods or professionals right when the party needs them. Think of TP like a video-game resource: you earn them through specific skills and spend them to trigger powerful, commerce-flavored effects.

HOW TO TRACK (Foundry V12)

  • On your Actor, add a numeric Resource named Trade Points (TP) and show it on the sheet.
  • Increase/decrease this value as skills award or consume TP. (There’s no default reset—only the listed skills change the total.)

HOW TO GAIN TP

WINDS OF TRADE — Rest Gain & Cap

After you rest in an area where commerce is possible, you gain 【SL + 1】 TP. You can never hold more than 【SL + 3】 TP. If you start play with this Skill, begin the campaign with 2 TP.

REAL TREASURE — Session Reward

Prerequisite: You have acquired Winds of Trade.
Once per session, when you help an NPC or a community defeat greed and corruption, improve their quality of life, or coexist with other creatures, you gain 【SL + 1】 TP.

WHAT TO SPEND TP ON

I’VE HEARD OF IT! — Quick Expertise Boost (Cost: 1 TP)

When you or an ally who can hear and understand you makes a Check to examine a creature, item, or location, spend 1 TP to grant a bonus equal to 【SL × 2】 to the Result of that Check.

PRIVATE STOCK — Cover Small Purchases (Cost: 1 TP)

When you or another Player Character would spend 【SL + 2】 or fewer Inventory Points, spend 1 TP to ignore that IP cost entirely.

WINDS OF TRADE — Market Conjuration (Cost: 2 TP, Non-Conflict Scene)

During a non-conflict scene, spend 2 TP and choose one option:

  • Material or Rare Item: Create a GM-approved good whose value in zenit is ≤ 【your level × 30】.
    (Flavor it as finding a supplier, expediting shipping, or revealing a “just-in-time” stash.)

  • Professional Contact: An NPC living nearby appears; you explain how you know them and their trade. The GM tells you what they require in exchange for their services.

QUICK REFERENCE

PLAY EXAMPLES

  • Scouting a ruin: The Scholar examines an ancient seal. You spend 1 TP with I’ve Heard of It! to add 【SL × 2】 and crack the puzzle.
  • Supply run on a timer: Before a big dungeon push, you spend 2 TP (non-conflict scene) via Winds of Trade to source a rare antidote worth ≤ 【level × 30】.
  • Covering costs: The Warrior needs quick supplies totaling 【SL + 2】 IP. You spend 1 TP with Private Stock so nobody pays IP.

DESIGN NOTES & TIPS

  • Theme: TP rewards ethical commerce and community uplift (see Real Treasure), not hoarding wealth.
  • Tempo: Plan rests in towns, markets, caravans, guild halls, or any locale where “commerce is possible” to refuel TP with Winds of Trade.
  • Party Support: Your boosts and freebies make everyone shine—Merchants are enablers and accelerators.

props.class_lore:
Even in worlds rife with great magic, wealth and money are very influential. Trade and commerce are one key aspect to the development of nations and kingdoms, and Merchants are quite aware of this power.

It might seem strange for a Merchant to be treated on par with a hero: and yet, those who resist the temptation of greed and rely on commerce to foster exchanges of ideas and dialogue between distant people truly are fighting their very own revolution.
